dataset_example.question: How does Holmes regard emotions and love, and in what way is Irene Adler an exception to his usual stance?
dataset_example.answer: Holmes regards emotions—especially love—as abhorrent intrusions that would disturb his perfectly balanced reasoning, likening them to grit in a sensitive instrument; nevertheless Irene Adler is uniquely remarkable to him—“the” woman who eclipses all others in his eyes, though he claims no romantic attachment and remembers her only as being of “dubious and questionable memory.”

items.answer: Turner explained that McCarthy had preyed on him for years after recognizing him from their criminal gang in Ballarat, extorting land, money, and influence; when McCarthy pressed his son to marry Turner’s daughter and thus threaten her future and his legacy, Turner—already dying and haunted by his past—killed McCarthy to protect Alice and to break McCarthy’s power over him. His former life as “Black Jack of Ballarat” made him both fearful of exposure and fiercely determined to prevent his daughter from marrying into McCarthy’s line.
